title: Luke 1:1–2: many undertook; the Church keeps four
english: On [[Luke 1:1 >> Bible:Luke 1:1]] — Since many undertook to set out a narrative of the things fulfilled among us — Origen hears a fitting apology: for a human to write Gods teaching is an oversized attempt. As Israel once had true and false prophets sorted by discernment of spirits, so many wished to write Gospels, yet approved bankers did not take every coin. Undertook may quietly blame those who rushed to record without the gift. Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John wrote moved by the Spirit; Egyptian, Twelve, and Basilides gospels were mere undertakings. The Church prefers only the four.

Fulfilled, not merely believed, marks what cannot be broken. Matters strikes down those who say the Saviors deeds were only appearance. Luke received the story as [[eyewitnesses and servants of the Word >> Bible:Luke 1:2]] handed it down from the beginning.
